steps.what: Check the class rules and permitted escalation route
Observe behaviour and judge whether intervention is needed
Remind, redirect and de-escalate with pupils
Write and verify required behaviour incident notes
Save the approved incident note

tasks.design: Pin the approved class rule sheet in {DOCS} and use the existing pupil-record category of {OTHER} for a short incident form. The teacher observes and intervenes personally; headings and class references reduce repeated incident-note entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Temporary teachers may receive rules separately from class information.
tasks.enabler_now: Native pinned links and incident forms can share a class context.
tasks.still_hard: Fair and proportionate responses in an unfamiliar classroom.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room and de-escalate without labelling a child.
tasks.altitude: Small lookup and note savings; classroom responsibility is unchanged.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-7 for temporary access, safeguarding and national consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: class-specific links and structured incident notes can reduce navigation and repeated headings; they do not enforce behaviour.

assumptions: Boundary includes rules lookup, live enforcement and required incident notes over a mix of ordinary and reportable events. No automated behaviour scoring, recording or sanctions.

School staff maintain class_id, rule_version and escalation_contact. s4 captures pupil_reference, time, witnessed_behaviour and response from the teacher's own observation. Missing fields retain manual lookup and prose.
Test native links/forms first. Shares are provisional work estimates, not prior buckets. No notes are invented for events not recorded today; confirm that baseline.
s5 is a near-zero native save represented by schema minimum 1%, fully retained. Gross 3.2%; upkeep 0.5 gives net 2.7%.
unknowns: Availability of a substitute rule sheet
research_questions: Do temporary-access controls expose only the assigned class?

already_counted.description: Write and check factual incident content

incremental.description: Report stale rule links and form issues

approvals.approved_version: approved incident note v1 including pupil and final factual text; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% with existing pinned rules and a short form and no deployment; 2% if access or form corrections consume 0.7 more baseline hours than central net 2.7%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Hear the question and clarify the pupil's difficulty
Consult lesson references and the teacher's answer key when needed
Develop and check an explanation suited to the pupil

loop.input: Teacher-entered anonymous question, lesson objective and selected source paragraph
loop.output: One explanation with a worked example and source pointer
loop.check: Teacher checks reasoning, example answer, age suitability and consistency with the lesson before using it
loop.stop: One suggestion; absent source or incorrect reasoning means teach from the original source manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Search supplies the facts; unfamiliar misconceptions can need a new explanation rather than a copied paragraph. Use direct lookup for routine factual questions.

steps.what: Explain the answer and check understanding with the pupil

tasks.design: Index the assigned lesson references in {DOCS} or {LMS} before adding any model. For difficult questions, a bounded draft can suggest an explanation from a selected source, but the teacher checks it and remains the person answering the pupil.
tasks.previous_blocker: A substitute may know the subject but not the absent teacher's chosen explanation or examples.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked retrieval and a short explanation draft can aid preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Misconceptions and age suitability require teaching judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Notice whether the pupil actually understands and adapt the live explanation.

ambition.what: Offer an alternative worked example to pupils not helped by the first explanation.

tasks.altitude: Less reference preparation; live teaching time and grading rights do not change.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10 for source access and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a source-grounded draft may help an unfamiliar teacher prepare an explanation; no pupil-outcome gain or time saving is measured here.

assumptions: Boundary is answering questions, including occasional reference consultation and explanation preparation. Shares describe a question mix, not every brief classroom reply. No pupil chatbot or automated assessment.

Absent teacher supplies lesson_id, objective, source text, source_version and answer_key. The substitute enters anonymous question and checks the result in s3; entry and checking are included in its 80% remaining time. Missing approved material means manual teaching, not open-ended generation.
Native source links and direct lookup come first. Only difficult explanations use a loop; central reductions assume modest average gains across the question mix.
Gross 7%; focal source/quality upkeep 0.8 gives central net 6.2%. No live conversation time is reduced.
unknowns: Whether tool latency fits classroom use
research_questions: Does explanation preparation remain faster after typing and checking?
Are suggested examples logically correct and suitable for the class?

already_counted.description: Capture anonymous question and check the explanation

incremental.description: Check source links and audit explanation failures

approvals.approved_version: approved explanation v1 with checked example; a changed explanation must be checked again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% for questions immediately answerable without tools, with no tool deployed; 5% when additional source checks consume 1.2 baseline hours beyond central net 6.2%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach from the absent teacher's lesson plan.

steps.what: Read the lesson sequence and intended outcomes
Locate the specified worksheets, slides and equipment
Deliver the planned instruction and learning activities
Manage activity transitions and adjust pacing to class progress
Write and verify the lesson-coverage handover note
Save the approved coverage note

tasks.design: Use the existing {LMS} lesson page to link the absent teacher's plan and specified materials. A coverage checklist reuses activity headings for the substitute's factual handover; reading, teaching and pacing remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plan attachments and lesson materials may be separated.
tasks.enabler_now: Native lesson pages and activity-linked notes reduce navigation and repeated headings.
tasks.still_hard: An unfamiliar class may need a different pace without abandoning the learning goal.
tasks.human_edge: Judge class understanding while following another teacher's intentions.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less material retrieval and handover typing; no new curriculum rights.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5 for substitute access and national consultation if applicable

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: lesson pages can link existing materials and reuse activity names in coverage notes.

assumptions: Boundary is plan execution and coverage handover. Dedicated pupil questions, behaviour incidents and attendance are separate tasks and must not be added again to the lesson denominator.

The absent teacher's existing preparation supplies lesson_id, activity_id, sequence, material_reference and plan_version. Missing links mean manual retrieval. s5 manually supplies actual completion and deviations; planned activities never stand in for actual coverage.

Test native lesson-page configuration first. Physical equipment retrieval within s2 retains effort; its 30% reduction applies only to digital reference navigation. Confirm that digital share before rollout.
s6 is a near-zero native save, minimum 1% fully retained. Gross 4%; upkeep 0.5 gives central net 3.5%.
unknowns: Whether activity-linked coverage notes already exist
research_questions: Can substitutes access the materials without broader pupil-record access?

already_counted.description: Record and check actual lesson coverage

approvals.approved_version: approved coverage note v1 including actual completions and deviations; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% with already-linked materials and notes, with no deployment; 3% when broken links cost 0.5 extra baseline hours beyond central net 3.5%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take attendance and maintain the class register.

steps.what: Open the correct class roster for the session
Call names or visually confirm pupils present
Enter observed attendance statuses in the register
Resolve late arrivals, unfamiliar names and uncertain statuses
Check the complete register and approve final statuses
Commit the approved attendance register

tasks.design: Configure a session-specific register view in the pupil-record category of {OTHER}, with keyboard or multi-row marking of pupils actually observed. The teacher resolves uncertainty and approves the entire register before committing it; absence messages are outside this design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Substitute access can require navigating several class screens and opening each pupil row.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scoped views and multi-row status entry may remove repeated clicks.
tasks.still_hard: Correctly identifying pupils and accounting for late arrivals.
tasks.human_edge: Confirm who is present rather than treating a timetable as evidence.
tasks.altitude: Less register navigation; attendance accountability remains with the substitute.

reach.learn: Attendance codes and correction audit trails

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-7 for temporary permissions and applicable national consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a session-scoped register with multi-row entry can reduce repeated clicks without detecting attendance automatically.

assumptions: Boundary is observation, register entry, correction and commit. No facial recognition, pupil self-service or parent messaging.

School records staff already maintain pupil_id, class_id, enrolment_dates and session_id. s2 produces observed presence; s3 explicitly captures status and observed_time. Missing roster membership or ambiguous names remain manual in s4.
Test native view and entry controls first; never pre-mark presence from planned enrolment. No saving if the register already supports this flow.
s6 is a near-zero same-system save at minimum 1%, fully retained. Gross saving 8%; focal upkeep 0.5 gives central net 7.5%.
research_questions: Does multi-row entry reduce clicks without increasing wrong-pupil statuses?

already_counted.description: Verify the final observed attendance register

approvals.approved_version: approved attendance v1 binding session, roster and final statuses; any correction requires renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 0% for an already-efficient register and no change; 6% if access and membership issues consume 1.5 more baseline hours than central net 7.5%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Protect classroom interaction while reducing repeated retrieval and register entry.
reach: Support records clerks with resolved attendance discrepancies
Offer tutor-style explanations for unfamiliar misconceptions
role.ambitious_version: A substitute who follows the intended lesson, answers questions reliably and leaves accurate attendance and coverage records.
